newsitem.title: INDIA: Mixed response seen for issue of India's BPCL.
newsitem.headline: Mixed response seen for issue of India's BPCL.

text.p: India's state-run refining firm Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), unfazed by a downtrend in the primary market since January, announced on Tuesday the pricing of its 4.12 billion rupee equity issue.
Each share of 10 rupee face value would be priced at 275 rupees, a BPCL spokesman said.
Analysts said BPCL would have no problem in selling about half the issue reserved for institutional buyers, but may have problems in selling the remainder to retail investors.
"We think it will be difficult to sell the issue at the retail level," said an executive of a securities firm.
"We suggested a price band of 200-225 rupees when a merchant banker interviewed us," he said.
BPCL touched a low of 220 rupees on the Bombay Stock Exchange in recent months. On Tuesday, it was trading around 279 rupees.
Analysts said one factor which could help BPCL would be that retail investors could pay in four instalments. This meant the public issue would be only 500 million rupees at a time, they said.
But this also meant retail investors could sell their shares only after one year.
A similar public issue of shares by Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) had attracted sizeble subscriptions from companies last year.
"This year, corporates may not have funds like last year," one analyst said.

Domestic institutions, banks and mutual funds have been reserved 20 percent of shares and foreign institutional investors and non-resident Indians another 20 percent. Employees have been alloted 10 percent.
The issue would reduce the government's holding in BPCL to 60.18 percent from 66.2 percent. The issue would partly finance BPCL's capital expenditure of 57.2 billion rupees up to the year 1999/2000.
"It is the first good issue to hit the market after a long time," said a broker. "Every FII (foreign institutional investor) has a buy on it," he said.
BPCL is one of India's three leading refiners with a market share of 20.3 percent during 1995/96 (April-March). Its Bombay refinery refines 7.2 million tonnes of crude annually.
